trajectory_summary: The call is a long, low-energy technical slog: roughly 20 of its ~23 minutes are spent trying to get one screenshot of a kilowatt-usage graph off a ComEd account, with the same cost-vs-usage confusion repeated three times. The rep eventually secures the data and books a next-day appointment, but the customer attaches a live competitive-shopping caveat in the same breath, making the booking real but fragile.
outcome_dispute: This should be read as a booked-but-conditional appointment, not a clean win. A day/time (tomorrow at 2PM) was explicitly locked, so it is not merely tentative — but the customer's own words ('I don't wanna make no commitment... I got somebody else coming') attach a structural condition to it that the rep never resolved, closer to protocols-style conditional booking than a clean close.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (2PM, confirmed at 23:05-23:07) were locked with an in-person specialist visit, meeting the booked bar, though the customer's own price-shopping caveat at 20:56 makes this a fragile rather than clean booking.

The flip should have landed around 02:37 ('Yeah. No. We can we can definitely help you get that cut down.') by connecting the specific dollar jump to what the appointment will fix.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: This is a follow-up call ('this is Holland again... following up about that solar request') picking up mid-process rather than a fresh intro, so the rep never explicitly asks what interested the customer in solar; the closest proxy is the bill-jump disclosure, which functions as an implicit reason but was never solicited or reinforced as such.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: The one that you sent me was actually for your costs and not your actual kilowatt usage.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep repeats the identical cost-vs-usage correction three times over 16 minutes despite two earlier proofs (04:56, 12:47) that the customer could read bill numbers aloud successfully. Per bill_collection.alternative_paths.elderly_low_tech_protocol, the pivot to verbal read-back should happen within 2 minutes of friction, not 15+ — this single fix would have cut the call roughly in half.
